festival.title: El Paso Parish Announced an October 3-4 Lebanese Festival
festival.body: Saint Sharbel Maronite Catholic Mission in El Paso announced a Lebanese Festival for October 3 and 4, 2026, with Lebanese food, live entertainment and dabke dancing. Those advertised dates have passed. This card preserves the original announcement, not a post-event report; attendance and the event outcome have not been verified.
festival.source: Parish announcement: Saint Sharbel Maronite Catholic Mission
anniversary.title: Emmitsburg Celebrates Nine Years of Saint Sharbel's Shrine
anniversary.body: The Family of Saint Sharbel USA reports that pilgrims gathered on September 26 at the National Shrine Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes in Emmitsburg, Maryland, for the ninth anniversary of Saint Sharbel's shrine dedication. The celebration included Eucharistic Adoration, confessions and Mass celebrated by Father Theodore Trinko, IVE, at St. Mary's Glass Chapel. After Mass, pilgrims followed the saint's relic in procession to the shrine, where they received a blessing with Saint Sharbel's oil and venerated the relic. The organizer published its account on September 30.
anniversary.source: Family of Saint Sharbel USA: anniversary account (September 30, 2026)

consecration.title: Beirut Cathedral Consecrates an Altar to Blessed Patriarchs Douaihy and Hoayek
consecration.alt: Saint George Maronite Cathedral in downtown Beirut, with the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque beside it
consecration.caption: Saint George Maronite Cathedral (left) and the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, downtown Beirut, 2009. Venue context, not the consecration Mass. Photo: Lebnen18, CC BY-SA 3.0; WebP conversion.
consecration.body: On Sunday, September 27, Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Bechara Boutros Al-Rahi presided over the consecration of an altar dedicated to Blessed Patriarchs Estephan Douaihy and Elias Hoayek at Saint George Maronite Cathedral in downtown Beirut, with the two patriarchs' relics placed within it. President Joseph Aoun attended, alongside religious and official figures and faithful from across Lebanon, especially Zgharta-Ehden, Douaihy's birthplace region. In his homily, Al-Rahi paired the two blesseds: Douaihy "preserved the church's memory and heritage amidst persecution," while Hoayek "carried the nation's cause amidst major transformations." Both remain Blessed, not canonized saints: Douaihy was beatified in 2024, Hoayek on July 25, 2026.

kfifan.title: Saint Charbel's Formation Monastery Receives Relics from Rome
kfifan.body: Kfifan's Monastery of Saints Cyprian and Justina received relics of its two patron saints from Rome, MTV Lebanon reported on October 2. Mass, a blessing and a procession marked their feast. Father Emile Akiki of the Lebanese Maronite Order led the Mass. Saint Charbel studied at Kfifan before his ordination, under Saint Nimatullah Al-Hardini. The report also recalls the monastery's connection with Blessed Estephan Nehme. These are relics of Cyprian and Justina, not Saint Charbel. The ceremony's exact calendar date is not specified.

galleryNews.title: From the Historic Photograph to a New Saint Charbel Art Series
galleryNews.intro: We have added an AI transformation series to our gallery, bringing the historic photograph of Saint Charbel into conversation with new devotional art. The original stays visible beside the renditions, so visitors can see the source and the artistic choices for themselves.
galleryNews.process: The collection shows the work as a series, from imagined portraits to close portraits and a comparison strip. The current first candidate has a dark beard with a grey center streak; the window portrait also has a dark beard. Other takes remain visible, so visitors can compare different artistic choices rather than seeing one image presented as a definitive likeness. The final and alternate renditions use the historic photograph as their reference; the early candidates are imagined portraits, not verified transformations of that source photograph.
galleryNews.honesty: We are proud to share the series, and we want its meaning to be clear. These are AI-assisted artistic renditions, not newly discovered photographs, a reconstruction of a documented scene or proof of an apparition. The gallery labels the new images as artistic renditions or "AI transformation, not a photograph." The historic photograph remains separately identified and credited. A personal-experience caption on the first candidate is presented as the website creator's own account, not independent verification.
galleryNews.invite: Explore the series in our gallery: open an image full-screen, compare the original and the renditions, and read the caption beside each piece.

tour.title: Lebanese and Jordanian Ministers Visit Saint Charbel's Pilgrimage Sites
tour.body: Lebanon's Tourism Minister Laura Al-Khazen Lahoud and Jordan's Tourism and Antiquities Minister Imad Hijazin visited Qozhaya monastery, Bqaa Kafra, Annaya and Saint Charbel's hermitage on Friday, according to the National News Agency's October 3 report. They met priests and monks and were briefed on Lebanon's religious trails, including the Lebanon Mountain Trail and the trail associated with Saint Charbel. The report describes a visit and briefing, not a new agreement or a trail opening.

opening.title: Mar Charbel Listed for October 22 Opening in Beirut
opening.body: Beirut Souks Cinemacity now lists October 22, 2026 as the opening date for Mar Charbel, the 130-minute biopic directed by Nadim Mehanna. Its film page has no screening sessions scheduled yet. Lebanon24 reported on October 5 that the film would begin showing in Lebanese cinemas on October 22 after an earlier postponement; its account of booking demand cites an unnamed source. The cinema listing supports the planned opening date, not a completed release, a confirmed showtime or an international rollout.

premiere.title: Charbel Premieres in Beirut; Lebanese Cinema Release Set for October 22
premiere.body: Charbel, the new feature film about Saint Charbel, held its special premiere on October 9 at BlackBox in Beirut Media Zone, according to Nidaa al-Watan's October 10 report. The film is a joint NMPRO and MTV production, directed by Nadim Mehanna and written by Claudia Marshalian, with Jerry Ghazal playing the young Charbel and Father Roukoz El Hajj portraying him later in life. Cinemacity lists a runtime of 130 minutes.
premiere.release: Lebtalks reported that the October 9 launch was under President Joseph Aoun's patronage and would be broadcast on MTV, with a nationwide Lebanese theatrical rollout planned from October 22. Cinemacity Beirut independently lists Thursday, October 22 as its opening date. Its page still has no screening sessions scheduled. The completed premiere and the upcoming public cinema opening are different milestones.
premiere.scope: A separate charity screening in support of Anta Akhi is scheduled for October 12 at ABC Achrafieh. International release dates, streaming distribution and English-language availability remain unconfirmed.
